paper.title_en: Scalar superradiance in the charged black-bounce spacetimes
paper.abstract_en: We numerically investigate the superradiant amplification effect of a charged scalar field in the scattering experiment and the black hole bomb model in a charged black-bounce spacetime. Due to the shallowing effect on the effective potential by the introduced quantum parameter $ł$, superradiance in both the above cases is verified to be weakened. In a scattering experiment, the quantum parameter and the field mass suppress the amplification in all frequency ranges, while the black hole and field charge suppress the amplification at low frequencies but enhance it at high frequencies. In a Type I black hole bomb model, where the reflective mirror is placed outside the ergo-region, we find a new distinct eigen-mode for the scalar field evolution in a high $ł$ value, which is however absent in the light-particle sub-case of the Type II black hole bomb where the mirror is set inside the ergo-region. Moreover, we investigate the heavy field mass scenario in a Type II black hole bomb, in which an additional eigenfrequency emerges at the same high $ł$ value but is not superradiantly amplified.
